title: Pick the shelf liner that stops a glass sliding on a 20-degree drying rack
instruction: Select a suitable liner, lay it on the fixed 20 degree rack, stand one glass on it, release both glass and liner, and leave both hands off for 20 seconds after 0.5 seconds settling, with at most 5 mm displacement and 15 degree normal misalignment.
context: Shelf liners of smooth vinyl, rubber and open-cell foam can look the same yet grip a glass very differently, and the only way to know which one will hold is to try it. Here six grey liners look alike apart from their number dots, and nothing visible tells them apart; only testing reveals which ones grip a glass well enough at 20 degrees, where a bare glass slides off the varnished rack. The task is choosing the liner by testing, not just laying down a mat.
setup: One fixed layout. World frame: x forward, y left, z up; table top at z = 0.7475 m. Six grey liner samples, numbered one to six by white dots, each 70 x 150 x 6 mm and 75 g, lie flat at (x, y, z) = (0.07, 0.05, 0.7505), (0.07, -0.05, 0.7505), (0.07, -0.15, 0.7505), (0.26, 0.05, 0.7505), (0.26, -0.05, 0.7505) and (0.26, -0.15, 0.7505) m. They are smooth vinyl/PVC, rubber or open-cell foam with estimated, hidden dry and wet friction against glass, and they look alike. Two glass tumblers (cylinders 74 mm diameter x 70 mm tall, 200 g) stand at (0.10, -0.28, 0.7830) and (0.24, -0.28, 0.7830) m. A fixed wooden rack board, 340 x 240 x 12 mm, centred at (0.65, -0.05, 0.8479) m and sloped 20 degrees along x, stands on four 24 mm square legs; it has no retaining lip, and its varnished surface (friction 0.3) is too slippery to hold a bare glass. A shallow metal pan (140 x 170 mm opening, 4 mm floor, 35 mm walls, reference centre (0.435, -0.05, 0.7475) m) holds 20 mm of water; a liner dipped in it becomes wet and switches to its wet friction, which for some liners is much lower. A loose wooden practice board, 180 x 140 x 8 mm and 400 g, lies at (0.70, 0.25, 0.7515) m. The pan, the second glass and the practice board are optional: the robot may use them, for example to try a liner before committing, but this task needs only one glass and does not require wetting. Two six-joint YAM arms with parallel grippers sit on metal supports (120 x 240 mm footprint, 148.9 mm tall): left base at (0.36, 0.20, 0.8975) m with yaw -90 degrees, right base at (0.40, -0.36, 0.8975) m with yaw +90 degrees. Exact per-object dimensions and transforms are in candidate/task.py and candidate/c1_contract.py.
scoring: 0.25 for a liner lying on the rack: touching the rack and not the table, its normal within 15 degrees of the rack normal, and not supported by the robot through the loose board or other liners. 0.5 when a released glass stands on exactly one such liner, touches neither the bare rack nor the table or other furniture, has its axis within 15 degrees of the rack normal, and is not supported by the robot through any movable chain of contacts (including the other glass). After 0.5 s of settling, the glass centre must stay within 5 mm of where it settled: 0.75 after 10 s and 1.0 after 20 s without interruption. If the glass moves more than 5 mm, that placement is void until the robot places it again. All credit is lost if a glass tips more than 60 degrees from vertical, slides more than 10 mm below the rack's low edge, or falls more than 30 mm from where the robot last held it onto the table or other furniture; also if a wrist force stays above 80 N for 0.1 s, or if a required measurement is invalid. Otherwise 0.
run_limit: 2,268 steps (113.4 seconds at 20 Hz), including settling and the full hold
reset_notes: Reset restores all objects to their fixed start poses, every liner to its dry material, and clears contact, force, damage and hold history and the step budget. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid liners and solid glass cylinders (glass centre of mass 7 mm below centre). Glass-liner friction uses dedicated colliders so each pair keeps its own dry or wet value. Liner compression is a 6540 N/m spring, not a material model. Water is visual; a liner inside the water volume switches once to its wet friction, with no fluid simulation. Arm torque limits including gravity: 27 N m (joints 1-3), 7 N m (joints 4-6), 40 N per finger; non-finger contact force uses a conservative Coulomb bound.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,268 steps); demo: 1.0 (1,469 steps, glass held hands-off for 25.3 seconds)
